days.name: Sun 02/08
days.weather_detail: Sunny (89%), wind 19 mph (gusts 44 mph), 0% precip. Bitter cold.
days.dinner_description: Classic Philly cheesesteaks with paper-thin ribeye from RD, seared screaming-hot on a cast-iron griddle until the edges crisp and the fat renders. Provolone melted directly over the beef, sautéed onions caramelized until sweet, all piled into garlic-butter-toasted hoagie rolls.
days.dinner_notes: Pick up steak from RD beforehand. Quick cook — sear thin slices at high heat.
days.album_description: Born in a Tottenham warehouse studio full of vintage gear and Tabasco-bottle percussion, Franc Moody's debut is pure London disco-funk energy. Ned Franc and Jon Moody spent 18 months crafting these irresistibly funky tracks — they're playing 9:30 Club on Feb 19 if you catch the bug.
days.album_sonic_description: Disco-funk basslines, shimmering synths, falsetto vocals, infectious hooks
days.album_pairing_rationale: Cheesesteaks are a contact sport — hot griddle, fast hands, melted cheese flying. You need music with the same energy. Franc Moody's disco-funk basslines turn the kitchen into a dance floor while you sear.
days.activity: Cozy indoor day — board games or movie afternoon
days.activity_notes: Too cold for outdoor activities (17°F with 44 mph gusts). Hunker down.

prep_steps: Partially freeze ribeye for thin slicing
Slice onions and peppers
Sear beef at high heat 90 sec per side
Melt provolone over meat on griddle
Toast hoagie rolls and assemble
prep_detail.make_ahead: Slice meat and prep veggies ahead of time.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Worcestershire Fond Glaze
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: During the last 30 seconds of cooking the beef, hit it with a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce directly on the screaming-hot griddle. Let it sizzle and caramelize into the meat. This creates a savory glaze that makes the steak taste more like steak.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Worcestershire adds umami depth (anchovies, tamarind) without anyone detecting individual flavors. It browns into the fond and coats each slice.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Garlic Butter Roll Toast
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Melt 2 tbsp butter with 1 minced garlic clove. Split hoagie rolls, brush the insides with garlic butter, and griddle cut-side down until golden and crisp. The butter creates a moisture barrier that prevents the bread from going soggy.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Garlic butter adds flavor and creates a crispy, waterproof barrier between bread and juicy filling. Restaurant cheesesteaks always toast the roll — home versions rarely do.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Crispy Shallot Rings
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Thinly slice 2 shallots into rings. Toss in seasoned flour, shake off excess, and fry in 350°F oil for 2-3 minutes until deeply golden. Drain on paper towels, salt immediately. Pile on top of the assembled cheesesteak.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Adds crunchy textural contrast to the soft, melty sandwich. The shallot sweetness echoes the caramelized onions but in crispy form.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Quick-Pickled Hot Peppers
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Slice banana peppers or cherry peppers into rings. Cover with equal parts white vinegar and water, a pinch of sugar and salt. Let sit 15 minutes. Pile onto cheesesteaks for a bright, acidic crunch.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Acid cuts through the richness of beef and melted cheese. The vinegar bite resets your palate between bites so the last one tastes as good as the first.

days.day_intro: It's 17°F with wind gusts up to 44 mph — the kind of Sunday where you don't leave the house unless someone's on fire. Which makes it the perfect day for cheesesteaks, board games, and Franc Moody's disco-funk warming the kitchen like a space heater with a bassline.

days.name: Mon 02/09
days.weather_detail: Sunny (90%), wind 8 mph, 0% precip. Cold but calm.
calendar_items: Conduit Demonstration and Planning 4:00-5:00 PM (Reston Conf Room 5.1B)
days.dinner_description: Eggs poached in a smoky, garlicky tomato sauce spiked with harissa and finished with cold labneh dollops and a shower of za'atar. The contrast between the searing-hot sauce and the cool yogurt is what separates this from 'eggs in tomato sauce.' Serve with thick-cut sourdough for dunking — the yolk situation demands it.
days.dinner_notes: One-skillet, 20 minutes. Perfect after a long office day.
days.album_description: Chicago drummer and producer Makaya McCraven doesn't just play jazz — he deconstructs and reassembles it with a hip-hop producer's ear. 'In These Times' layers live ensemble recordings with lush strings and vibraphone into something warm, unhurried, and impossible to stop playing.
days.album_sonic_description: Live jazz ensemble cut-and-pasted with hip-hop sensibility, lush strings, vibraphone
days.album_pairing_rationale: After a full office day, you need music that doesn't ask anything of you but gives everything back. McCraven's meditative grooves match shakshuka's one-skillet simplicity — both are layered, warm, and better than they have any right to be for something so effortless.

prep_steps: Sauté onions and peppers in olive oil
Add garlic, cumin, paprika
Pour in crushed tomatoes, simmer 10 min
Create wells, crack in eggs
Cover and cook 5-7 min until whites set
Crumble feta on top, serve with bread
prep_detail.make_ahead: Tomato base can be made ahead and reheated.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Harissa Swirl
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Stir 1-2 tsp of harissa paste into the tomato sauce before adding eggs. Then dot another teaspoon on top in small spoonfuls and drag a knife through for a marbled effect. The harissa blooms in the heat.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Harissa adds smoky, complex heat that's more interesting than just adding cayenne. The visual swirl makes the dish look restaurant-worthy.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Za'atar and Lemon Finish
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: The moment the skillet comes off heat, sprinkle 1 tsp za'atar over the eggs and squeeze half a lemon across the whole dish. Add a few torn mint leaves.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Za'atar's dried herbs and sesame cut through the tomato richness. The lemon juice brightens everything just before serving — this is the step restaurants never skip.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Cold Labneh Dollops
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Drop 3-4 tablespoons of cold labneh (or thick Greek yogurt) in dollops around the hot shakshuka right before serving. Don't stir it in. The cold-hot contrast is the point.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Cold labneh against searing-hot tomato sauce creates a temperature contrast that makes every bite different. The tang of labneh also balances the sweetness of cooked tomatoes.

days.day_intro: Monday at the office with a demo running until 5 PM. By the time you walk in the door, you want something that requires exactly one pan and zero decisions. Shakshuka delivers — eggs, spiced tomatoes, feta, bread, done.

days.name: Tue 02/10
days.weather_detail: Sunny (87%), 80% cloud cover, wind 7 mph, 1% precip. Warmest day of the week.
time_constraints: Swim lessons in the evening — need a fast dinner before or after
days.dinner_description: Silky fettuccine Alfredo made the Roman way — no cream, no shortcuts. Just good butter, a mountain of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, and the starchy pasta water doing the heavy lifting to create a glossy emulsion that clings to every strand. Finished with a snowfall of lemon zest from 12 inches above the bowl — the aromatic citrus oil brightens everything without breaking the sauce.
days.dinner_notes: Quick comfort food before swim lessons. Use Babo brand pasta.
days.album_description: Say She She is a Brooklyn trio channeling the shimmering three-part harmonies of 70s disco-soul through a modern indie lens. 'Prism' sounds like Chic and Rotary Connection had a baby and raised it on Afrobeat. They're at 9:30 Club on Feb 17 — two days before Franc Moody hits the same stage.
days.album_sonic_description: Three-part harmonies, vintage disco production, funk guitar, Afrobeat percussion
days.album_pairing_rationale: Pasta night needs warmth without drama. Say She She's vintage disco-soul provides exactly that — the three-part harmonies float over the simmering butter like steam rising from the pot. Groovy enough to keep energy up before swim lessons.
days.activity_notes: Elsie swim lessons in the evening

prep_steps: Boil salted water, cook fettuccine until al dente
Reserve 1 cup pasta water before draining
Melt generous butter in warm pan
Toss hot pasta with butter, add Parmigiano in batches
Splash pasta water as needed for silky sauce
Serve immediately
prep_detail.make_ahead: Have cheese grated and butter measured. Speed is key.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Toasted Garlic Chip Garnish
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Slice 4-5 garlic cloves paper-thin. Slowly cook in 2 tbsp olive oil over medium-low heat, swirling constantly, until light gold — about 3 minutes. Remove immediately to a paper towel. They'll darken as they cool. Reserve the garlic oil.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Garlic chips add textural crunch to an otherwise uniformly soft dish. The reserved oil can be drizzled on top for another layer of flavor without disturbing the emulsion.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Lemon Zest Snowfall
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Using a Microplane, zest one lemon directly over each plated bowl of Alfredo from about 12 inches above. The zest should fall like snow. Do not squeeze the lemon — you want fragrance, not juice.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Rich Alfredo needs a counterpoint. Lemon zest adds bright, aromatic citrus oil without the acid that would break the emulsion. It's the restaurant secret for Alfredo that doesn't taste heavy.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Cracked Black Pepper and Toasted Breadcrumbs
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Toast 1/4 cup panko in butter until deep gold. Season with flaky salt. Crack pepper aggressively — you want visible flecks. Serve both tableside.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: The breadcrumbs give crunch against silky pasta. The pepper adds heat that cuts richness. Together they prevent 'Alfredo fatigue' — that heaviness by bite five.

days.day_intro: The warmest day of the week at 48°F — practically spring by this week's standards. But swim lessons mean the evening is a sprint: home, cook, eat, go. Babo Alfredo is the answer — 20 minutes, four ingredients, infinite comfort.

days.name: Wed 02/11
days.weather_detail: Sunny (90%), 52% cloud cover, wind 13 mph, 18% precip.
days.dinner: Kale Caesar Salad with Crispy Chickpeas
days.dinner_description: Lacinato kale — the sturdy, blue-green variety that doesn't wilt into nothing — massaged with olive oil and lemon until tender, then tossed in a proper anchovy-lemon Caesar dressing with shaved Parmesan, herbed croutons, and chickpeas roasted with cumin and smoked paprika until they shatter when you bite them. This isn't a side salad. This is dinner.
days.dinner_notes: Hefty dinner salad. Roast chickpeas with cumin and smoked paprika for crunch and protein.
days.album: Hiroshi Yoshimura – Music for Nine Post Cards
days.album_description: Originally commissioned for Tokyo's Hara Museum of Contemporary Art in 1982, Yoshimura's debut is nine pieces of pure stillness — sparse electric piano and warm analog synths that were designed to merge with the museum's architecture, not compete with it. The 2017 reissue introduced it to a global audience who immediately understood: this is music you live inside.
days.album_sonic_description: Sparse piano, warm analog synths, silence as instrument, environmental music
days.album_pairing_rationale: A clean, bright salad dinner needs clean, airy music. Yoshimura's crystalline ambient doesn't fill a room — it reshapes it. The silence between notes is as intentional as the lemon in the dressing. Both are exercises in restraint that somehow feel abundant.
days.activity: WFH flex day — maybe an afternoon walk if weather holds
days.activity_notes: 45°F is the warmest this week — take advantage if possible
prep_notes: Massage kale with olive oil and lemon juice 30 min before serving

prep_steps: Roast chickpeas with cumin and smoked paprika at 425°F for 25 min
Strip kale from ribs, tear into pieces
Massage kale with olive oil and lemon juice
Make Caesar dressing: mash anchovy with garlic, whisk in egg yolk, lemon, mustard, olive oil, Parmesan
Toss kale with dressing
Top with croutons, chickpeas, and shaved Parmesan
prep_detail.make_ahead: Chickpeas can be roasted ahead. Dressing keeps 3 days in fridge.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Warm Anchovy-Garlic Oil Drizzle
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Gently warm 3 tbsp olive oil with 2 chopped anchovy fillets and 1 sliced garlic clove over low heat until the anchovies dissolve — about 3 minutes. Drizzle this warm oil over the dressed kale just before serving.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Warm oil on cool kale creates a temperature contrast and blooms the anchovy flavor. The garlic in the oil echoes the garlic in the dressing but in a softer, sweeter form.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Parmesan Frico Shards
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Mound 2-tbsp piles of grated Parmesan on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake at 400°F for 5-6 minutes until golden and lacy. Cool completely — they'll shatter into crispy shards. Stand them upright in the salad.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Frico adds dramatic visual height and a shattering crunch that standard shaved Parmesan can't match. Same ingredient, completely different experience.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Preserved Lemon Dice
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Dice 1 tbsp preserved lemon rind very finely. Scatter over the salad. If you don't have preserved lemon, mix lemon zest with a pinch of salt and let sit 10 minutes.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Preserved lemon adds a fermented, floral acidity that's more complex than fresh lemon. It's the difference between a chord and a single note.

days.day_intro: Midweek reset. No meetings, working from home, 45°F outside. This is the day to take an afternoon walk, massage some kale, and let the week breathe. A big, punchy Caesar salad for dinner because not every night needs to be heavy — sometimes the salad is the main event.

days.name: Thu 02/12
days.weather_detail: Sunny (92%), 87% cloud cover, wind 13 mph, 11% precip.
days.calendar: Valentine's Day potluck lunch at work
calendar_items: Valentine's Day potluck lunch (bring heart-shaped mini pizzas)
time_constraints: Big lunch at work — lighter appetite for dinner
days.dinner: Mushroom Pappardelle with Fresh Egg Pasta
days.dinner_description: Wide ribbons of fresh egg pappardelle — the kind you can only get by making it yourself, with that tender, silky chew — tossed with a mix of cremini, oyster, and rehydrated porcini mushrooms seared until deeply golden in brown butter with crispy sage. The porcini soaking liquid gets reduced to a syrup and stirred in — it's liquid umami. Finished with toasted walnuts and a splash of sherry vinegar you'll barely taste but absolutely miss if it's gone.
days.dinner_notes: Make the fresh egg pasta dough in the afternoon and rest it. Roll and cut wide pappardelle before dinner.
days.album_description: Mulatu Astatke was the first African student at Berklee College of Music. He took what he learned about jazz and Latin music and fused it with Ethiopian pentatonic scales and traditional modes to invent an entirely new genre: Ethio-jazz. 'Mulatu of Ethiopia' (1972), recorded in New York, is the masterwork — vibraphone, organ, and congas moving through hypnotic minor-key grooves that sound like nothing else ever recorded.
days.album_sonic_description: Ethiopian pentatonic scales, vibraphone, organ, congas, walking bass, jazz arrangements
days.album_pairing_rationale: Earthy mushroom pappardelle and earthy Ethio-jazz — the pairing writes itself. The vibraphone's warm shimmer mirrors the brown butter, the walking bass echoes the deep umami of reduced porcini, and the hypnotic repetition matches the meditative rhythm of rolling fresh pasta.
days.activity_notes: Bring heart-shaped mini pizzas for the potluck
prep_notes: Make fresh pasta dough Thursday afternoon, rest 30 min

prep_steps: Make pasta: 2 cups 00 flour + 3 eggs, knead 10 min, rest 30 min
Rehydrate dried porcini in hot water, reserve liquid
Slice cremini and oyster mushrooms
Roll and cut wide pappardelle ribbons
Brown mushrooms in butter over high heat
Deglaze with white wine and porcini liquid
Cook pappardelle 2-3 min in salted water
Toss pasta with mushrooms, add Parmesan and sage
prep_detail.make_ahead: Pasta dough can be made morning and rested in fridge.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Brown Butter with Crispy Sage
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: In a separate small pan, cook 4 tbsp butter over medium heat until it foams, goes quiet, then turns nutty brown — about 4 minutes. Drop in 8-10 sage leaves and fry 30 seconds until crisp. Pour the brown butter over plated pasta. Set crispy sage leaves on top.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Brown butter adds a toasted, nutty complexity that regular melted butter cannot. The milk solids caramelize. Crispy sage is a textural garnish and a flavor intensifier.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Porcini Soaking Liquid Reduction
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Strain the porcini soaking liquid through a coffee filter to remove grit. Reduce it by half in a small pot. Add this concentrated mushroom liquor to the sauce when you deglaze with white wine. It's liquid umami.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Dried porcini soaking liquid is one of the most concentrated sources of natural glutamate available. Reducing it intensifies the effect. This is the 'why does this taste better than normal' ingredient.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Toasted Walnut Crumble
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Toast 1/3 cup walnut halves in a dry pan until fragrant. Roughly chop. Scatter over plated pasta with a grinding of black pepper.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Walnuts add a bitter, tannic crunch that echoes the earthiness of the mushrooms. Italian tradition pairs walnuts with fresh pasta — this is why.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Sherry Vinegar Finish
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Just before tossing the pasta into the mushroom pan, add 1 tsp good sherry vinegar to the sauce. Toss immediately. The vinegar will mostly evaporate, leaving behind complexity.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Earthy mushroom dishes need a hidden acid to prevent them from tasting flat. Sherry vinegar adds nutty acidity that complements both the brown butter and porcini without tasting 'vinegary.'

days.day_intro: Thursday pulls double duty: Valentine's heart-shaped mini pizzas for the potluck lunch at work, then home to make fresh egg pasta from scratch for dinner. The pappardelle is the week's cooking project — hands in flour, dough resting, mushrooms browning — and it's worth every minute.

days.name: Fri 02/13
days.weather_detail: Sunny (92%), 39% cloud cover, wind 11 mph, 22% precip.
time_constraints: Laura at book club — Dan solo dinner duty
days.dinner_description: Butterflied bronzino roasted at 425°F over a bed of lacinato kale, burst cherry tomatoes, and white beans — the fish makes its own pan sauce from lemon, garlic, and good olive oil as it cooks. Scored skin with thyme tucked into the slashes, finished under the broiler for two minutes until the skin crackles. Topped with a crispy caper and lemon zest gremolata that adds brightness and crunch to every bite.
days.dinner_notes: Can prep the kale-tomato-bean bed ahead. Nestle fish on top when home from picking up Elsie. 25 min in oven.
days.album_description: Laufey (pronounced 'Lay-vay') is an Icelandic-Chinese jazz-pop prodigy who studied cello at Berklee before becoming the youngest artist ever to win the Grammy for Best Traditional Pop Vocal Album. 'Bewitched' blends golden-age jazz sensibility — think Chet Baker, Ella Fitzgerald — with bossa nova rhythms and Gen-Z lyrical honesty. It's intimate, romantic, and quietly sophisticated.
days.album_sonic_description: Jazz guitar, gentle strings, bossa nova rhythms, intimate vocals
days.album_pairing_rationale: Light fish, light music. Laufey's bossa nova-inflected jazz is airy enough for delicate bronzino and romantic enough for the night before Valentine's Day. The intimacy of her voice — close-miked, almost whispered — matches the intimacy of a solo dinner with your daughter.
days.activity_notes: Dan solo with Elsie after 6 PM. Quick dinner, cozy evening.
prep_notes: Prep kale-tomato-bean bed before picking up Elsie

prep_steps: Preheat oven to 425°F
Tear kale, toss with olive oil and garlic on sheet pan
Add halved cherry tomatoes and drained white beans
Roast vegetables 10 min
Nestle butterflied bronzino on top, season with salt, pepper, lemon
Roast 15-18 min until fish flakes
Finish under broiler 2 min for crispy skin
prep_detail.make_ahead: Kale, tomatoes, and beans can be prepped and arranged on the pan hours ahead. Fish goes on right before baking.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Ladolemono (Greek Lemon-Olive Oil Sauce)
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Whisk 1/4 cup best olive oil with juice of 1 lemon, 1 minced garlic clove, 1 tsp dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Spoon generously over the fish the moment it comes out of the oven. The heat emulsifies the sauce.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Ladolemono is the Greek answer to 'what sauce goes with fish.' The heat from the fish partially cooks the garlic and blooms the oregano. Simple, devastating.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Score and Stuff the Fish
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Score the skin of the butterflied bronzino with 3 diagonal slashes on each side. Tuck thin lemon slices and thyme sprigs into the slashes. This looks dramatic and allows heat and seasoning to penetrate evenly.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Scoring prevents the skin from curling during high-heat roasting and lets the aromatics infuse directly into the flesh. It also promotes crispier skin.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Crispy Caper and Lemon Zest Gremolata
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Pat dry 2 tbsp capers. Fry in olive oil for 1 minute until they bloom open and turn crispy. Mix with finely grated lemon zest and 1 tbsp chopped parsley. Scatter over the plated fish.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Fried capers are crunchy, briny, and addictive. Combined with lemon zest and parsley, this gremolata adds brightness and crunch to the soft, flaky fish.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Room-Temperature Tomato-Bean Salad Base
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Toss the roasted cherry tomatoes and white beans with a splash of red wine vinegar while warm, then let them cool to room temperature before plating under the hot fish.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Serving the bean-tomato bed at room temperature against hot, crispy-skinned fish creates a pleasant temperature contrast and lets the vinegar-brightened beans serve as a sauce.

days.day_intro: Friday is a split operation: Elsie at YAT until 6, Laura at book club. Dan picks up Elsie, comes home, and slides a prepped sheet pan of bronzino into a hot oven. Twenty-five minutes later: crispy-skinned fish over roasted kale, and the whole evening ahead for just the two of them.

days.name: Sat 02/14
days.weather_detail: Sunny (92%), 5% cloud cover, wind 7 mph, 20% precip. Clearest day of the week.
time_constraints: Travel day — prep enchiladas ahead or assemble on arrival
days.dinner_description: Enchiladas divorciadas — the dramatic 'divorced' presentation with rich red guajillo-ancho chile sauce on one side and bright tomatillo-green chile sauce on the other. Corn tortillas quick-fried for pliability and flavor, filled with shredded chicken and cheese, topped with crema, Cotija, cilantro, pink pickled red onions, and toasted pepitas. The two sauces meet in the middle of the baking dish like a delicious peace treaty.
days.dinner_notes: Travel day — can prep filling and sauces Friday night. Assemble and bake on arrival.
days.album_description: There's a reason Sade's 'Love Deluxe' (1992) is the only album anyone ever needs for Valentine's Day. 'No Ordinary Love' opens with a bass line that sounds like a heartbeat. 'Kiss of Life' is the kind of song that makes you slow-dance in the kitchen. The whole record moves with the confidence of someone who knows exactly what they're doing — smoky, elegant, and impossibly cool.
days.album_sonic_description: Smooth jazz, quiet storm R&B, African rhythms, silky vocals, saxophone
days.album_pairing_rationale: It's Valentine's Day. There is exactly one album. Sade's smoky sophistication turns enchiladas from a casual dinner into a candlelit event. The African rhythms underneath the quiet storm R&B mirror the Mexican warmth of the dish. No debate, no alternatives.
days.activity_notes: Travel day. Keep it simple and romantic.
prep_notes: Prep enchilada filling and sauces Friday night

prep_steps: Shred rotisserie chicken or poach and shred chicken breasts
Make red sauce: toast dried chiles, blend with garlic and oregano
Make green sauce: roast tomatillos and green chiles, blend
Warm tortillas, fill with chicken and cheese, roll
Arrange in baking dish — red sauce one side, green the other
Top with more cheese, bake at 350°F for 15-20 min
Garnish with crema, Cotija, cilantro, and avocado
prep_detail.make_ahead: Filling and both sauces can be made a day ahead. Assemble and bake on site.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Toast and Fry the Tortillas
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Before filling, pass each corn tortilla through hot oil (350°F) for 5-8 seconds per side — just enough to make them pliable and slightly golden. This prevents them from going soggy under the sauce and adds a subtle fried corn flavor.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: The #1 mistake in enchiladas is using raw tortillas that absorb sauce and turn to mush. A quick oil pass creates a moisture barrier and adds flavor. Every Mexican grandma knows this.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Bloom the Dried Chiles Properly
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: For the red sauce: stem, seed, and dry-toast the chiles (guajillo + ancho) in a hot, dry skillet until they blister and become fragrant — about 30 seconds per side. Then soak in just-boiled water for 20 minutes. Blend with roasted garlic, oregano, and a splash of the soaking liquid.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Toasting before soaking develops complex smoky flavors that simply soaking cannot achieve. The Maillard reaction on the dried chile skin creates caramelized notes.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Quick-Pickled Red Onion Garnish
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Thinly slice 1 red onion into rings. Cover with lime juice, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of sugar. Let sit 20 minutes until bright pink. Pile on top of enchiladas after baking.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Pickled onion adds crunchy acid that cuts through the richness of melted cheese and crema. The pink color is stunning against the red and green sauces.

dinner_elevation_tips.title: Toasted Pepita Garnish
dinner_elevation_tips.instruction: Toast 1/4 cup raw pepitas (pumpkin seeds) in a dry skillet over medium heat, tossing frequently, until they puff and start to pop — about 3 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lime.
dinner_elevation_tips.why: Pepitas add an authentic Mexican crunch that complements the soft enchilada texture. Their nutty, slightly bitter flavor bridges the two sauces.

days.day_intro: Valentine's Day, the clearest sky of the week, and a travel day. The enchilada filling and both sauces are prepped from Friday night — all that's left is assembly and 20 minutes in a hot oven. The visual alone — half red, half green, topped with pink pickled onions — is a Valentine worthy of the occasion.

appetizers.name: Whipped Feta Dip with Roasted Red Peppers
appetizers.description: Creamy whipped feta blended with roasted red peppers, garlic, and a drizzle of good olive oil. Served with warm pita triangles and crudités.

appetizers.name: Crispy Baked Mozzarella Bites
appetizers.description: Golden panko-crusted mozzarella bites baked until molten inside, served with warm marinara. Kid-proof and party-ready.

salads.name: Winter Citrus & Radicchio Salad
salads.description: Composed plate of blood orange and cara cara segments, shaved radicchio, burrata, toasted pistachios, and Castelvetrano olives.
salads.dressing: Blood orange vinaigrette: fresh blood orange juice, champagne vinegar, Dijon mustard, extra-virgin olive oil, minced shallot, flaky salt, cracked black pepper
salads.flavor_rationale: Bitter radicchio tamed by sweet citrus and creamy burrata. Pistachios add crunch. Italian amaro-dolce-grasso balance.

salads.name: Shaved Brussels Sprout Slaw with Apple & Pecans
salads.description: Thinly shaved Brussels sprouts with Honeycrisp apple matchsticks, toasted pecans, dried cranberries, and Pecorino Romano.
salads.dressing: Apple cider vinaigrette: apple cider vinegar, whole-grain mustard, honey, extra-virgin olive oil, salt, pepper
salads.flavor_rationale: Brussels sprout bitterness against sweet apple and tart cranberries. Pecans add warmth. Vinaigrette keeps it crisp and lively.

salads.name: Roasted Beet & Citrus Salad with Goat Cheese
salads.description: Earthy roasted beets with grapefruit and orange segments, tangy goat cheese, and toasted walnuts on arugula.
salads.dressing: Sherry-walnut vinaigrette: sherry vinegar, Dijon mustard, walnut oil, extra-virgin olive oil, minced shallot, honey, salt, pepper
salads.flavor_rationale: Earthy beets and bright citrus in sweet-savory tension. Goat cheese adds tang, walnuts bring warmth. Valentine's-worthy colors.

beverages.name: Malbec (Red Wine)
beverages.description: Full-bodied, plummy Malbec from Mendoza — the ideal companion for a beef-heavy week. $12-15 range.
beverages.why: Pairs with cheesesteaks, pappardelle, and enchiladas.

beverages.name: Sparkling Pomegranate Mocktail
beverages.description: Pomegranate juice, fresh lime, simple syrup, and sparkling water over ice. Festive ruby-red.
beverages.why: Non-alcoholic option for the family. Valentine's-worthy color.

beverages.name: Japanese Lager (Asahi or Sapporo)
beverages.description: Crisp, clean Japanese lager served ice-cold. Cuts through rich miso or umami flavors.
beverages.why: Light contrast to the umami-heavy bronzino and kale dinner.

prep_ahead: Saturday: Pick up ribeye from RD for Sunday cheesesteaks
Wednesday night: Make pizza dough for Thursday potluck heart pizzas
Thursday morning: Shape and bake heart-shaped mini pizzas for potluck
Thursday afternoon: Make fresh egg pasta dough, rest 30 min
Friday afternoon: Prep kale-tomato-bean bed for bronzino
Friday evening: Prep enchilada filling and both sauces for Saturday
notes: Beef craving satisfied on Sunday (cheesesteaks) and Thursday (pappardelle mushrooms with richness).
Valentine's heart-shaped mini pizzas for Thursday work potluck — Gen Alpha approved.
Thursday potluck is lunch; mushroom pappardelle for dinner balances the day.
Kale and bronzino+kale give two hearty kale nights as requested.
Saturday is travel day — enchilada components travel well, assemble on arrival.

This week tells a story in temperatures — from 17°F Sunday to the week's warmth on Tuesday (48°F) and back down again. The dinners follow suit: hearty bookends with lighter, brighter cooking in the middle.

Two kale nights (Wednesday and Friday) might sound repetitive on paper, but they're completely different experiences — a punchy Caesar versus a Mediterranean fish supper. The green thread ties the week together.

weekly_theme.title: Love in Action
weekly_theme.description: Valentine's week isn't just about cards and candy — it's a chance to explore what love looks like when it's a verb. How do we show care through cooking together, through small kindnesses at school, through making someone's favorite meal? This week, look for moments to ask Elsie: what does love look like when you do it, not just say it?

dinner_questions.question: If you could make any sandwich in the world for your best friend, what would you put on it and why?
dinner_questions.why: Connects food to friendship and generosity. At 8, she's deeply invested in best-friend dynamics — this lets her express care through a creative, low-stakes scenario.

dinner_questions.question: What's the bravest thing you saw someone do today — even if it was something small?
dinner_questions.why: Eight-year-olds are building their moral compass and starting to notice courage in everyday actions. This question helps her practice recognizing bravery beyond physical feats — standing up for someone, trying something new, admitting a mistake.

dinner_questions.question: If our family had a theme song, what would it sound like? Fast or slow? Loud or quiet? What instruments?
dinner_questions.why: Swim lesson nights are rushed — this question is pure fun with no right answer. It invites creativity and reveals how she perceives the family's energy. Plus, there's music playing (Say She She) — she can riff off what she hears.

dinner_questions.question: What's something you're really good at that you didn't used to be good at? How did you get better?
dinner_questions.why: At 8, she's developing a growth mindset — the ability to see effort as the path to mastery. This question helps her narrate her own competence story, which builds resilience for future challenges.

dinner_questions.question: Valentine's Day is coming up — if you could show love to someone at school without using words, how would you do it?
dinner_questions.why: This ties directly to the weekly theme of 'love in action.' It pushes her to think about non-verbal expressions of care — saving a seat, sharing a snack, drawing a picture. These are the building blocks of empathy.

dinner_questions.question: What's something you wish grown-ups understood better about being 8?
dinner_questions.why: This is a trust question. It says: I want to understand your world. Eight-year-olds often feel unheard by adults — this invites her to be the expert. Listen without correcting.

dinner_questions.question: What are three things you love about our family — not things we have, but things we do?
dinner_questions.why: Valentine's Day dinner — the perfect moment to talk about family love. Asking about actions (not possessions) reinforces that love is demonstrated, not just felt. Travel day makes this a great car conversation too.

nudges.title: The Sous Chef Moment
nudges.context: Thursday's dinner involves making fresh pasta from scratch — eggs, flour, and rolling. This is the perfect invitation.
nudges.suggestion: Let Elsie handle the pasta dough. Crack the eggs, measure the flour, knead until smooth. Don't correct her technique unless she asks. Let the mess happen.
how_to: Set up her station: apron, flour, eggs, a clean surface
Show her once how to make the well and crack the eggs in
Step back. Let her knead. Let her feel the dough change texture.
When it's smooth, tell her: 'You made that. From scratch. That's real.'

nudges.title: The Valentine Card Factory
nudges.context: Valentine's Day is Saturday but the potluck is Thursday. The week is naturally Valentine-themed — lean into it with a creative project early in the week.
nudges.suggestion: Monday or Tuesday evening, set out supplies and make Valentine cards together — not store-bought, handmade. For friends, for teachers, for each other.
how_to: Gather: construction paper, markers, stickers, scissors, glue
Each person makes at least 3 cards — including one for each family member
No templates or Pinterest perfection — messy is better
Read them aloud to each other before sealing

nudges.title: The Friday Solo Mission
nudges.context: Laura is at book club. Dan is solo with Elsie after YAT pickup at 6 PM. This is a connection goldmine.
nudges.suggestion: After dinner, let Elsie choose the entire evening agenda. Movie, game, craft, or just talking. The only rule: no phones for either of you. Call it 'Elsie's Night.'
how_to: On the drive home from YAT, ask: 'Tonight is yours. What do you want to do?'
Whatever she picks, commit fully. Don't suggest alternatives.
If she picks a movie, watch it next to her, not across the room.
Before bed: 'I really liked hanging out with just you tonight.'

recommendation.title: Each Kindness
recommendation.author: Jacqueline Woodson
recommendation.why: A beautiful picture book (yes, even for 8-year-olds) about a girl who misses the chance to be kind to a new student — and the regret that follows. It's short, powerful, and unforgettable. Perfect for Valentine's week because it reframes love as everyday kindness, not grand gestures.
recommendation.connection: Ties directly to the 'Love in Action' theme. Read it together any night this week — it takes 10 minutes and will generate a conversation that lasts much longer.

parenting_data.parent_reflection: This week, pay attention to how Elsie shows love — not how she says it. Does she save you the best piece? Does she draw you a picture unprompted? Does she sit closer to you on the couch? Those small, wordless gestures are her love language developing in real time. Notice them. Name them. 'I saw you saved me the corner piece — that made me feel really loved.' She needs to know her love lands.

nutrition_summary: This week's dinners are hearty and satisfying — exactly what a cold February demands. Protein variety is outstanding (beef, eggs, dairy, chickpeas, fish, chicken across seven nights), and the two kale-forward dinners provide serious nutrient density midweek. The gaps are what you'd expect from comfort cooking: no whole grains at dinner, limited fruit, and some rich nights. The fix is easy — whole grain lunches, fruit-heavy snacks, and a vitamin D supplement while February keeps the sun at bay. Overall grade: B+, and the lunches and snacks below bring it to an A.

protein_diversity.notes: Outstanding protein variety — 5 distinct animal sources plus plant-based (chickpeas). Red meat, fish, poultry, eggs, and legumes all represented. Well distributed across the week.

vegetable_coverage.notes: Three dinners have abundant vegetables (shakshuka, kale Caesar, bronzino+kale), but Sunday and Tuesday are very low. The two kale nights help significantly. Lunches need to carry vegetables on low-veg days.

nutrient_gaps.detail: Zero dinners include whole grains — all starches are refined (hoagie roll, white pasta x2, corn tortillas). Lunches and snacks must compensate.
Only Wednesday (chickpeas, kale) and Friday (beans, kale) provide meaningful dinner fiber. Other nights are refined-carb heavy.
No fruit appears at any dinner — entirely normal, but lunches and snacks must provide 2-3 daily fruit servings.
Friday's bronzino and Thursday's mushrooms provide some vitamin D, but February sunshine is limited. Consider supplementation.

excesses.detail: Sunday (beef+cheese), Tuesday (butter+Parmigiano), and Saturday (cheese+crema) are all rich. Balanced by lighter Wed-Fri dinners.
Every dinner with a starch uses refined carbs. Not a crisis, but whole grain lunches would help balance blood sugar and fiber.

fiber_assessment.notes: Wednesday and Friday are fiber-rich; other nights are low. Weekly dinner fiber averages ~8g/dinner — below ideal. Whole grain lunches and fruit snacks are essential.

omega3_assessment.notes: Friday's bronzino provides omega-3 fatty acids. One fish dinner per week meets minimum recommendations. Add walnuts or flaxseed at breakfast for extra coverage.

weekly_assessment.overall_summary: This is a genuinely well-balanced dinner week with standout protein variety and some excellent nutrient-dense nights (Wednesday's kale Caesar and Friday's bronzino are nutritional powerhouses). The gaps — whole grains, fiber, and fruit — are entirely normal for dinner menus and easily filled through lunches and snacks. The heavier nights (Sunday, Tuesday) are balanced by lighter, vegetable-forward nights midweek. Valentine's week comfort food without nutritional guilt.

recommended_lunches.name: Whole Grain Turkey & Avocado Wrap
recommended_lunches.description: Whole wheat tortilla with sliced turkey, mashed avocado, shredded carrots, spinach, and a squeeze of lemon. Roll tightly and slice in half.
recommended_lunches.kid_notes: Elsie can help roll her own. Skip the spinach if she resists — the carrots and avocado carry the nutrition.

recommended_lunches.name: Lentil Soup with Crusty Bread
recommended_lunches.description: Red lentil soup with carrots, cumin, and lemon — make a big batch Sunday and portion for the week. Serve with a slice of whole grain bread.
recommended_lunches.kid_notes: Red lentils dissolve into a smooth, creamy soup that kids love. It doesn't look 'beany' — big win.

recommended_lunches.name: Mediterranean Grain Bowl
recommended_lunches.description: Quinoa or farro with cucumber, cherry tomatoes, olives, feta, and a lemon-olive oil dressing. Add rotisserie chicken for Dan's portion.
recommended_lunches.kid_notes: Let Elsie build her own with toppings she likes. Feta and olives are usually kid-winners.

recommended_lunches.name: PB&J on Whole Wheat + Fruit Side
recommended_lunches.description: Classic peanut butter and strawberry jam on whole wheat bread with a side of apple slices or clementines.
recommended_lunches.kid_notes: The eternal school lunch. Reliable, portable, and nutritionally solid with whole wheat.

recommended_lunches.name: Chicken Caesar Salad Wrap (Leftover Wednesday Dressing)
recommended_lunches.description: Use leftover Caesar dressing from Wednesday. Toss with romaine, grilled chicken strips, and Parmesan. Wrap in a whole wheat tortilla.
recommended_lunches.kid_notes: Kids who eat Caesar salad at dinner will eat it in a wrap at lunch. Smart leftover play.

recommended_lunches.name: Hummus & Veggie Plate with Pita
recommended_lunches.description: Hummus with carrot sticks, cucumber rounds, bell pepper strips, and whole wheat pita triangles. Add olives and cherry tomatoes for adults.
recommended_lunches.kid_notes: Most 8-year-olds love dipping. Hummus is a stealth nutrition vehicle — chickpeas, tahini, lemon.

recommended_snacks.name: Apple Slices with Almond Butter
recommended_snacks.description: Sliced Honeycrisp apple (use leftover apples from the Brussels sprout slaw) with 2 tbsp almond butter.

recommended_snacks.name: Greek Yogurt with Honey and Walnuts
recommended_snacks.description: Plain Greek yogurt with a drizzle of honey and a handful of toasted walnuts (save some from the pappardelle elevation).

recommended_snacks.name: Clementines (No Prep Required)
recommended_snacks.description: 2-3 clementines. That's it. Portable, mess-free, and bursting with vitamin C.

recommended_snacks.name: String Cheese + Whole Grain Crackers
recommended_snacks.description: 2 string cheese sticks with a handful of whole grain crackers. Zero thought required.

recommended_snacks.name: Trail Mix (DIY)
recommended_snacks.description: Mix almonds, dried cranberries (leftover from salad), dark chocolate chips, and pumpkin seeds (leftover from enchilada garnish). Bag in portions.

recommended_snacks.name: Banana with Peanut Butter
recommended_snacks.description: One banana, halved lengthwise, spread with peanut butter. Can freeze for a treat.

recommended_snacks.name: Pomegranate Seeds (Valentine's Snack)
recommended_snacks.description: A bowl of fresh pomegranate seeds — ruby-red for Valentine's week. Buy a container of pre-seeded arils to save time.

nutrition_data.weekly_nutrition_summary: With these lunches and snacks supplementing the dinner menu, the family achieves solid coverage across all major nutrient categories. Whole grain gaps are filled by lunch wraps, pita, and crackers. Fruit intake jumps from zero (dinner-only) to 2-3 daily servings through snacks and lunch sides. Calcium coverage improves significantly with Greek yogurt, string cheese, and feta at lunch. The one remaining consideration is vitamin D — February in Virginia means limited sun exposure, and only two dinners (bronzino, mushrooms) provide meaningful vitamin D. A daily supplement of 600-1000 IU for all family members is a smart winter insurance policy.
special_notes: Consider a vitamin D supplement (600-1000 IU) for all family members during February — limited sunshine and indoor time make it hard to meet needs through food alone.
Elsie's swim lessons and YAT mean she's burning extra calories Tuesday and Friday — make sure she has a hearty after-school snack those days (trail mix + string cheese, or banana with PB).
Dan's Thursday potluck lunch will be heavy — the lighter mushroom pappardelle dinner is a good balance. He may want to go easy on snacks that afternoon.
The grocery list already includes walnuts, pecans, and chickpeas — repurpose leftovers into snacks to minimize waste and extra shopping.

highlight: Valentine's week in the kitchen: from Philly cheesesteaks on a bone-cold Sunday to Sade spinning over Christmas enchiladas on the 14th — seven nights of comfort, curiosity, and love in action.
